'''M. Christina White''' is a professor of chemistry at the [[University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign]].  Her research in the field of [[organometallic]] [[catalysis]] focuses on developing highly selective [[carbon–hydrogen bond activation]] methods to streamline the process of complex molecule synthesis.<ref>{{cite web | url = http://chemistry.illinois.edu/faculty/Christina_White.html | title = M. Christina White / Faculty / Chemistry at Illinois | accessdate= January 22, 2012}}</ref>

==Education==
White received a B.A. degree with highest honors in biochemistry from [[Smith College]] in 1992, where she worked with [[Stuart Rosenfeld]] in the area of [[host–guest chemistry]]. From 1992 to 1993, she worked in the biology graduate program at [[Johns Hopkins University]] with [[Christian Anfinsen]] on thermophilic bacteria protein folding. In December 1998, she earned her PhD in [[organic chemistry]] from [[Johns Hopkins University]] as an ACS Medicinal Chemistry Pre-Doctoral fellow, working with [[Gary H. Posner]]. Her doctoral research involved synthesis of hybrid [[vitamin D3|vitamin D<sub>3</sub>]] [[structural analog|analogs]].<ref>{{cite web | url = http://scs.illinois.edu/white/files/WHITE.MC.CV.2017.pdf | title = M. Christina White Curriculum Vitae / Chemistry at Illinois | accessdate= February 20, 2018}}</ref>

==Career==
In 1999, White joined [[Eric Jacobsen (chemist)|Eric Jacobsen]]'s labs at [[Harvard University]] as an [[NIH]] postdoctoral fellow. During this time, she developed the first synthetically useful [[methane monooxygenase]] (MMO) mimic system for catalytic [[epoxidations]] with [[hydrogen peroxide]]. In July 2002, White joined the [[Harvard University]] chemistry department as a faculty member. In 2005, she moved to Illinois, where she currently works at the [[University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign]] as a professor of chemistry, researching [[C–H bond activation]].<ref>{{cite web | title = White Research Group – M. Christina White | url = http://www.scs.illinois.edu/white/index.php?p=mcw_bio | accessdate = January 22, 2012}}</ref> White's notable students include [[Abigail Doyle]], of [[Princeton University]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://academictree.org/chemistry/tree.php?pid=57468|title=Chemistry Tree - M. Christina White Family Tree|website=academictree.org|access-date=2018-08-07}}</ref>

==Research==
White and her team aim to study and develop selective allylic and aliphatic C-H oxidation reactions for use in organic synthesis. White has contributed novel [[palladium]] / sulfoxide and [[iron]] catalysts that functionalize C-H bonds selectively, predictively, and without the need for directing groups.<ref>{{cite web | title = Videos of Eminent Organic Chemists – ACS Division of Organic Chemistry | url = https://www.organicdivision.org/eminentorganicchemists/m-christina-white/ | accessdate = February 20, 2018}}</ref> Her [[palladium]] / sulfoxide catalyst is referred to as the [[White catalyst|White Catalyst]], and her [[iron]] catalyst, Fe(PDP)(MeCN)<sub>2</sub>(SbF<sub>6</sub>)<sub>2</sub>, is referred to as the [[White-Chen catalyst]]; both catalysts are commercially available.<ref>{{cite web | title = White Catalyst – Sigma-Aldrich | url = https://www.sigmaaldrich.com/chemistry/chemical-synthesis/technology-spotlights/white-catalyst.html | accessdate = February 20, 2018}}</ref> Recent research in the White lab includes designing reactions for effecting non-directed, remote aliphatic C-H hydroxylation of simple amide-containing molecules.<ref>{{cite journal |author1=Nanjo, T  |author2=de Lucca, EC |author3=White, CM |name-list-style=amp | date = 2017 | title = Remote, Late-Stage Oxidation of Aliphatic C–H Bonds in Amide-Containing Molecules | journal = Journal of the American Chemical Society | volume = 139 | issue = 41 | pages = 14586–14591 | doi=10.1021/jacs.7b07665|pmid=28921954 |pmc=5812270 |bibcode=2017JAChS.13914586N }}</ref> White has also applied these catalysts and their derivatives to new applications, with the most recent being the White catalyst's [[dehydrogenation|dehydrogenative]] [[Diels-Alder reaction]]<ref>{{cite journal |author1=Stang, EM  |author2=White, MC  |name-list-style=amp | date = 2011 | title = Molecular Complexity via C–H Activation: A Dehydrogenative Diels–Alder Reaction | journal = Journal of the American Chemical Society | volume = 133 | issue = 38 | pages = 14892–14895 | doi=10.1021/ja2059704 | pmid=21842902 | pmc=3292869|bibcode=2011JAChS.13314892S }}</ref> and the iron-mediated intramolecular C-H [[amination]] reaction.<ref>{{cite journal |author1=Paradine, SM  |author2=White, MC  |name-list-style=amp | date = 2012 | title = Iron-Catalyzed Intramolecular Allylic C—H Amination | journal = Journal of the American Chemical Society | doi=10.1021/ja211600g | volume=134 |issue=4  | pages=2036–2039 | pmid=22260649|bibcode=2012JAChS.134.2036P }}</ref>
